clue.text: Really, shelter is in divine surroundings

indicators.note: the shelter word is said to be in what follows, so it sits inside the next piece
the divine word forms the surroundings, wrapping round the shelter word

parts.note: divine means holy
a nest is a shelter for birds

explanation.surface: Someone insists, with feeling, that a refuge stands in hallowed grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as an interjection of exasperated emphasis, a synonym pair as in 'Really, what next!'

clue.text: Make musical sound on instrument that's commonplace

parts.note: to hum is to make a musical sound with closed lips
a drum is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Playing a tune on an instrument that is quite ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means dull and ordinary, a synonym of commonplace.

clue.text: A croc isn't affected, given drugs

indicators.note: affected means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crocodile is unmoved despite being dosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges A CROC ISNT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are drugs, especially illegal ones; a synonym.

clue.text: Peter's kind of market

definitions.meaning: the comic actor Peter ..., so the surname that belongs to Peter
a market favouring vendors, where demand exceeds supply

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Sellers was the Goon Show actor, and a sellers' market is one where vendors hold the advantage.

clue.text: Trouble over one family member's affair

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned back, so the trouble word is reversed

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a family member

explanation.surface: Upset about a relative's romantic entanglement.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is an illicit romantic relationship, a synonym of affair.

clue.text: Business suffering setback in former site

indicators.note: the reversed business abbreviation is placed in the word for former

parts.note: late means former, as in 'the late chairman'

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the business abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A company that has hit trouble on the spot where it used to operate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to site something is to place or establish it in position, a synonym.

clue.text: Musical entertainment-see female look happy

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
a hen is a female bird
to grin is to look happy

explanation.surface: A show advertised with an invitation to watch a cheerful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is Wagner's opera, an example of a musical stage entertainment.

clue.text: Is rascal not able to spell?

parts.note: can't means is not able
a rip is an old word for a rogue or rascal

explanation.surface: A question whether a scamp cannot write words correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like spelling words; it is a magic charm, a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantrip is a Scottish word for a magic spell or a mischievous trick.

clue.text: Altered new lever on machine

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters of the previous word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A modified fresh lever fitted to a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' looks like the anagram signal; it is the fodder, and 'new' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that drives a machine such as a sewing machine.

clue.text: Walk round obscure out-of-date tube station

indicators.note: the walking word goes round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
blear is an archaic verb meaning to dim or obscure, hence out-of-date

explanation.surface: Strolling around some forgotten, disused Underground stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-date' looks like a description of the station, but it marks the obscure word as archaic. MARBLE ARCH is a London Underground station at the west end of Oxford Street, very much in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble Arch is an example of a London Underground (tube) station, on the Central line.

clue.text: Trotsky comes back for Christmas

indicators.note: coming back means the Trotsky name is read backwards

parts.note: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: The Russian revolutionary returns for the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is an old word for the Christmas season, familiar from carols.

clue.text: American Communist is chicken

parts.note: Rhode Island is an American state, so stands in for something American
red is a standard word for a Communist

explanation.surface: Calling a US leftist a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' reads as an insult meaning coward; it is the noun, the breed of hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhode Island Red is a well-known breed of domestic chicken, so this is an example.

clue.text: Part of the regime is sensitive in China

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that the government is touchy about part of its affairs in the People's Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is porcelain, and 'in China' means a kind of china.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is a celebrated German porcelain, so it is an example of fine china.

clue.text: English showing great enthusiasm for print

parts.note: raving means wildly enthusiastic, as in raving about a show

explanation.surface: An Englishman excited about a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print made from an engraved plate, so a synonym.

clue.text: Performer of monologue heard in cover version

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: a rapper delivers rhymed speech solo, a kind of monologue

explanation.surface: A hip-hop artist is heard on someone else's recording of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover version' suggests a re-recorded song; only 'cover' defines, with 'in' and 'version' joining.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering or casing that protects something is a synonym, like a sweet's paper casing.

clue.text: Snap decision making appointment with celebrity

parts.note: a snap is an informal word for a photograph
a call is a decision, as in a referee's call

explanation.surface: A hasty choice leads to a meeting with someone famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocall is an arranged occasion when a famous person poses for press photographers.

clue.text: Signal from State to vessel taking yonks

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine
SS stands for steamship, a vessel
yonks is British slang for a very long time, as is an age

explanation.surface: A communication from a government takes ages to reach a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yonks' is British slang for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a communication sent to someone, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Problems are raised for humanist

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so both pieces are reversed

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: Difficulties come up for a philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a leading Renaissance humanist scholar, so an example.

clue.text: Language originating in South West Africa has important linguistic implications

indicators.note: each word's origin is its first letter, so initials are taken

parts.words: South West Africa has important linguistic implications

explanation.surface: A claim that a tongue from southern Africa has significant linguistic consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originating in' takes the initials of South West Africa has important linguistic implications.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu language widely spoken in East Africa, an example of a language.

clue.text: Early centre of Christianity with a collection of writings and one old church

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of writings
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A city of the early Church described with its scriptures and ancient building.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch in Syria was where followers were first called Christians, an important early hub of the faith.

clue.text: Pains gone as I get treatment

indicators.note: treatment works on the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A patient's aches disappear after therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonies are severe pains, so a plural synonym.

clue.text: Leave the ground to become successful

definitions.meaning: what an aircraft does at departure
an idiom for suddenly doing well, as a career might

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both lift into the air and start to thrive.

clue.text: With nos. 3 and 4 out, Yorkshire changes into knitwear

indicators.note: changes means the remaining letters are rearranged into a new word
the third and fourth letters of the county name are removed

explanation.surface: A northern county side, missing two players, switches to woollens.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R and K from YORKSHIRE leaves YOSHIRE, which 'changes into' rearranges. Yorkshire is an English county with a famous cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery means stockings and socks, often knitted goods, so a loose synonym.

clue.text: How ships move very fast

definitions.meaning: a ship's speed is measured in nautical miles an hour
an idiom for at high speed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally gives a speed in nautical units and idiomatically means rapidly.

clue.text: I am joining good old-fashioned group of fighting men

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
PI, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: A speaker signs up with a decent traditional fighting band.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is crossword shorthand for pious, i.e. virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a Zulu regiment of warriors, a historical term for a body of fighting men.

clue.text: Give strength to prince captured by unruly native

indicators.note: the prince is held inside the rearranged native letters
unruly suggests disorder, so the letters of native are jumbled

parts.note: Prince Igor is the hero of Borodin's opera

explanation.surface: A royal seized by a rebellious local is told to buck up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges the fodder into INVATE, which 'captured by' wraps round the prince; Prince Igor is the title of Borodin's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate is to fill with energy, a synonym of giving strength.

clue.text: Making enquiries in the capacity of leader

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in 'acting as chair'
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: Someone asks questions while acting as head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking means putting questions, a synonym of making enquiries.

clue.text: To produce a benefit, leave no remnants

definitions.meaning: in a way that helps, an adverb
read as two words, use up entirely

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means helpfully, and split in two it means consume completely with nothing left.
